findings.title: Financial Services Commission emergency meeting on recent financial sector intrusion threats
findings.summary_md: South Korea's Financial Services Commission convened an emergency response meeting on October 2, 2026 with the Financial Supervisory Service, the Financial Security Institute, six banks and three card companies after the September 30 Shinhan Bank data leak and follow-on attacks on KB Kookmin Bank and other financial firms. The commission ordered immediate security reviews of internet-exposed systems and services, checks of authentication and access control, and rapid sharing of attacker IPs and methods with agencies including KISA. The statement did not name ARTEX.

findings.title: Financial sector hacking IOC: ARTEX AI public indicators and immediate checks
findings.summary_md: Plura Security published an IOC note on October 3, 2026 based on public reporting and analysis of ARTEX source code version 0.3.14. It lists three candidate User-Agent strings for WAF and log hunting: artex-enrich/1.0, Mozilla/5.0 (spa-api-recon) and Mozilla/5.0 (spa-api-recon spider), while cautioning that a User-Agent match alone does not prove compromise. The note also says the Financial Security Institute shared attacker IPs from the Shinhan Bank investigation with financial firms, and that some banks found overlapping attacker IPs.

findings.title: South Korean officials believe AI agents were used to hack several banks
findings.summary_md: The Record reported on October 6, 2026 that South Korean officials believed AI agents were used in hacks of at least seven financial institutions, with personal data of at least 68,000 people exposed. Officials had found 33 IP addresses linked to at least 12 countries, including Japan, the United States, Thailand, Vietnam and Hong Kong, and named Hana Bank, KB Kookmin Bank and Shinhan Bank among the victims. The incidents first came to light on September 30, 2026, and President Lee Jae Myung said AI made hacking easier without specialized skills.

findings.title: Three points to prepare for the successive unauthorized access attempts
findings.summary_md: GMO Cybersecurity by Ierae's cybercrime countermeasures lead wrote on October 15, 2026 that forensic logs from the breaches the firm handled made AI use almost certain, while noting that the breach at sister company GMO Research & AI ran on completely separate systems. The post focused on CVE blind spots, ASM gaps and WAF bypasses, including attackers rotating through hundreds of IP addresses to stay under WAF thresholds. It did not name ARTEX.

findings.title: Confirmed that many of the attack sources in the successive unauthorized accesses are AI
findings.summary_md: GMO Cybersecurity by Ierae confirmed on October 19, 2026 that ARTEX was present on attacker infrastructure it investigated, corroborating its earlier assessment that AI was used in the Japanese breach wave. The firm found about 20 Japanese companies targeted, nine of them in the same industry, and six additional AI attack servers focused on separate sectors. Eight of the targeted companies had already published breach notices in September and October 2026, and the firm shared the findings with law enforcement.
